timeline_events.summary: Mullah Omar vanished from view as US and Afghan forces toppled his Taliban government.
Ashraf Ghani was sworn in as president of Afghanistan in the first peaceful transfer of power since the fall of the Taliban in 2001.
The Taliban government in Afghanistan crumbled as Northern Alliance forces entered Kabul.
The US begins bombing Afghanistan to root out Osama bin Laden and his Taliban protectors.
Nato reported killing 94 Taliban fighters in the Kandahar region, bringing the toll from nine days of combat to more than 420 deaths.
NATO's top commander says the Taliban should not be blamed for all violence in Afghanistan, which is also being perpetrated by al-Qaida remnants and criminals.

Senior Whitehall officials warned that British troops in Afghanistan face the prospect of fighting the Taliban throughout the winter, and a truce brokered by local tribal leaders in Musa Qala district remained fragile.
Taliban leader Mullah Omar rejects President Hamid Karzai's peace talks overtures and says the Taliban intends to try Karzai in an Islamic court.
Taliban insurgency gains strength and sophistication, with suspicion falling on Pakistan over alleged support.
Up to 80 Taliban fighters were killed by Nato forces in a four-hour firefight in Helmand province, southern Afghanistan.
Western commanders expect a Taliban offensive to intensify as winter ends, presenting a major challenge to Nato forces in Afghanistan.
The Bush administration warns Somalia could become a new Taliban but has no intention of getting involved on the ground there.
A captured Taliban spokesman, Mohammed Hanif, alleges that Mullah Mohammed Omar is hiding in Quetta, Pakistan under the protection of the ISI, a claim Pakistan dismisses as "totally baseless."

Taliban spokesman Muhammad Hanif is captured and claims in a videotape released by Afghan authorities that Taliban supreme leader Mullah Omar is hiding in Quetta, Pakistan, and is protected by the ISI.
Taliban insurgents seized the town of Musa Qala in Helmand province, disarming local police and destroying government buildings.
The US was expected to urge NATO ministers at a meeting in Spain to launch a spring offensive against the Taliban in Afghanistan.
George Bush orders 3,200 extra US troops to Afghanistan in expectation of a spring offensive against a resurgent Taliban.
UK Defence Secretary Des Browne is expected to announce a deployment of over 1,000 extra British troops to Afghanistan to combat an expected Taliban spring offensive.

Pakistani security forces captured former Taliban defence minister Mullah Obaidullah Akhund in a raid in Quetta, though a Taliban spokesman denied the arrest and Pakistani officials did not confirm it.
A Taliban suicide bomber attacked Bagram air force base during a visit by US Vice-President Dick Cheney, killing at least 22 people, including an American soldier.
Two British soldiers were killed in a rocket attack during a Nato-led operation in Sangin, Helmand province, amid heavy clashes with Taliban fighters.
An Italian journalist, Daniele Mastrogiacomo, was kidnapped by the Taliban in Afghanistan's Helmand province along with his Afghan driver and translator.

British forces launched a major offensive, Operation Silicon, against Taliban forces in southern Afghanistan's Helmand province, as NATO reported US-led troops killed at least 136 suspected Taliban fighters in a separate attack in Herat.
Afghan MPs pass a draft law calling for talks with Afghan Taliban fighters and an end to international military offensives.
Taliban's top military commander Mullah Dadullah was killed during fighting with Afghan and Nato forces in Helmand province in southern Afghanistan.

Haji Mansour Dadullah, brother of slain Taliban commander Mullah Dadullah, claims in a television interview that he received a letter of condolence from Osama bin Laden, who is "alive, active and well."

A communications breakdown between US troops and Afghan security forces led to a US air strike that killed seven Afghan policemen who were mistaken for Taliban at a remote checkpoint in eastern Afghanistan.

The Taliban are increasingly gaining legitimacy as a political movement in southern Afghanistan by exploiting grievances over indiscriminate international force bombings and opium eradication, while also shifting to a guerrilla campaign of suicide bombings and assassinations in major cities.
The Afghan government threatens to use force against Taliban fighters holding 22 South Korean aid workers unless the 10-day kidnapping crisis is resolved quickly.
The Afghan government promises safe passage to two Taliban leaders for talks with South Korean negotiators on the fate of 21 hostages, according to the Taliban.

The UK Ministry of Defence confirms the deaths of three British soldiers from friendly fire when American F15 warplanes dropped a bomb on them during a clash between British forces and Taliban fighters in Helmand province, Afghanistan.
Taliban leader Mullah Brother was killed in an American-led pre-dawn raid in Helmand province, Afghanistan, according to the Afghan defense ministry.

Afghan President Karzai offers the Taliban a place in his government in return for peace and requests face-to-face talks with Mullah Omar and Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, while the Taliban refuse negotiations until all foreign forces leave Afghanistan.
Afghan police and western troops killed 20 Taliban fighters after surrounding two villages in Arghandab district, Kandahar province.
Nato troops plunged into a new round of fighting with the Taliban as hundreds of Afghan civilians fled villages around Kandahar, with about 50 militants reportedly killed.
Afghan, US and Canadian troops have surrounded around 250 Taliban fighters near Kandahar city and killed about 50 Taliban in three days of fighting in Arghandab.
A suicide bomb in northern Afghanistan, the deadliest attack since the Taliban's overthrow in 2001, strikes a blow to NATO and President Hamid Karzai's government.
A report by the Senlis Council says the Taliban has a permanent presence in 54% of Afghanistan and the country is in serious danger of falling into Taliban hands.

The Taliban carried out a suicide attack on a Nato convoy near Kabul's international airport, injuring at least 22 Afghan civilians, which a Taliban spokesman said was to welcome US defence secretary Robert Gates.

UK Prime Minister Gordon Brown stated he would not negotiate with the Taliban, while holding out the possibility that middle-ranking Taliban insurgents could renounce violence and join a political reconciliation process with Afghan President Hamid Karzai.

Afghanistan expels two Western officials, including a British UN official and an Irish EU adviser, for allegedly holding talks with the Taliban, which British and European officials call a misunderstanding.

Two senior Western officials, Michael Semple and Mervyn Patterson, face expulsion from Afghanistan after meeting tribal elders in Musa Qala, exposing divisions over whether the Taliban can be brought to the negotiating table.
Taliban militants attacked Kabul's Serena hotel, killing seven people and wounding six.
Paddy Ashdown accepts the role of UN envoy to Afghanistan, seeking a strengthened mandate to coordinate efforts against the Taliban insurgency.
The Taliban plan a spring offensive in Afghanistan.
The Taliban plan a spring offensive in Afghanistan.
A senior Taliban commander, Mansoor Dadullah, was captured after being seriously wounded in a gunfight near Zhob, in Baluchistan province, Pakistan.

A suicide bomber killed more than 80 people at a picnic spot in Kandahar, in the deadliest attack since the Taliban were ousted in 2001, with the Afghan government attributing the bombing to Taliban insurgents and their al-Qaida allies.

The Taliban are not being beaten and the insurgency is growing in intensity, while the PRT strategy of using aid as part of a counter-insurgency effort has failed and the Taliban increasingly target humanitarian aid workers as part of the occupation forces.

The Pakistani government signs a 15-point peace deal with Taliban militants in the Swat valley, agreeing to withdraw troops and introduce Sharia law in exchange for a halt to suicide bombings and attacks on government buildings.

The Taliban remain engaged in fighting in Afghanistan despite NATO efforts, with discussions emerging about potential negotiations contingent on the withdrawal of foreign troops and resolution of internal Afghan government divisions.
Taliban militants attacked Kandahar's main prison with a truck bomb and freed up to 1,000 prisoners, including 400 Taliban fighters.
Afghan President Karzai threatens to send troops into Pakistan to tackle Taliban operations.
Taliban forces overrun a series of villages in Arghandab district near Kandahar, three days after hundreds of fighters escaped from a Kandahar jail.

Taliban forces destroyed bridges and laid mines near Kandahar, prompting more than 4,000 people to flee villages and leading Afghan and Canadian forces to move into the region in anticipation of an attack.
Nato and Afghan forces killed 20 Taliban fighters in a major offensive on the outskirts of Kandahar, as British paratroopers deployed to the city to deter a potential Taliban threat.

Afghan defence officials claimed Taliban fighters occupying villages near Kandahar were forced to retreat by a major Afghan and Canadian Nato offensive, though Nato gave a more cautious assessment and did not confirm the death toll.

A suicide car bomber targeted the Indian embassy in Kabul, killing at least 41 people in the deadliest attack since the overthrow of the Taliban in 2001, though one Taliban spokesman denied responsibility while others appeared to contradict him.

Taliban militants attacked a remote US base in Kunar province, eastern Afghanistan, killing nine US soldiers and injuring 15 other NATO troops in one of the heaviest blows to coalition forces since 2001.
Pakistan suspends its military operation against insurgents in the Bajur tribal region for Ramadan, a decision welcomed by a Taliban spokesman.

A Human Rights Watch report states that civilian deaths in Afghanistan from US and NATO airstrikes nearly tripled over the past year, while the Taliban and associated militias continue suicide bombings and use civilians as human shields.
Two gunmen shot dead a high-ranking female police official in Kandahar, a former Taliban stronghold where she had resumed her job after US-led forces overthrew the Taliban government.

The international community is reportedly negotiating with the Taliban, with talks said to have been initiated by the Afghan government and backed by various international parties, and the Taliban putting forward demands including cabinet posts.
A UK commander says talks with the Taliban are the only way forward in Afghanistan.
US Secretary of Defence Robert Gates acknowledges that talks with the Taliban are necessary as part of a political outcome in Afghanistan.
More than 60 Taliban fighters were killed when NATO aircraft bombed a convoy as hundreds of insurgents launched a surprise attack on Afghan forces in Lashkar Gah, capital of Helmand province.
More than 60 Taliban fighters were killed when hundreds of insurgents attempted a surprise attack on Afghan forces in Lashkar Gah, Helmand province, and were pushed back by airstrikes.
Afghan President Hamid Karzai said he would guarantee the security of Taliban leader Mullah Mohammed Omar if he decided to enter into talks.
Taliban militants blew up five schools in north-west Pakistan, continuing a campaign against education.
Afghanistan postponed its presidential elections due to Taliban insurgency violence, with the vote rescheduled for 20 August.
The Pakistan Taliban blew up the school where Ali Khan taught in Charbagh, Swat, as part of its campaign against education.
Taliban militants launched a multi-pronged attack on government buildings in Kabul, killing at least 19 people and injuring 46, with the Taliban claiming responsibility.

The US ambassador to Afghanistan signals a new initiative to bring the Taliban into the Afghan political process, including discussing the formation of a political party or election candidates, alongside reinforced military efforts.

The Obama administration announced a new Afghanistan-Pakistan strategy recognizing that Taliban safe havens in Pakistan are largely responsible for Afghanistan's deteriorating situation and calling for low-level Taliban fighters to be persuaded to swap sides.
Heavily armed men in police uniforms stormed a police academy in Pakistan, killing 11 and injuring nearly 100, an attack claimed by Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan leader Baitullah Masud.
A new law supported by President Karzai is described as a grave step backwards for Afghan women's rights, despite progress since the fall of the Taliban.

Taliban fighters swept across Buner district, occupying government buildings and forcing local police to retreat, as Hillary Clinton warned the situation in Pakistan poses a "mortal threat" to world security.
Pakistani troops and helicopter gunships continued an assault on Taliban positions near the Swat valley, bringing the death toll from two days of fighting to nearly 50.
US coalition forces provided close air support during fighting between the Taliban and the Afghan National Army in Bala Baluk, Farah province, after an insurgent attack on an ANA group.

A US military investigation found that a failure to follow rules intended to prevent civilian casualties led to scores of Afghan civilian deaths during airstrikes against Taliban fighters in Farah province.
Pakistani helicopter gunships attacked Taliban-controlled positions in the Swat Valley, killing dozens of militants as fighting intensified.
Hillary Clinton expressed personal regret for civilian deaths as President Obama urged the Afghan and Pakistani presidents to step up attacks on Taliban and al-Qaida militants.
Pakistani security forces said they killed 64 Taliban fighters in the Swat valley and nearby Buner district.
Pakistan's government declares an end to peace initiatives with Taliban insurgents controlling Swat, signalling the start of a major military operation to drive the militants from the valley.
Pakistan’s military intensifies its campaign to dislodge the Taliban from the Swat Valley, with fighter jets striking Malam Jabba and clashes reported in Mingora.
A senior Pakistani army officer says the army has encircled the Taliban in strongholds across the Swat valley and will eliminate them, as the UN launches a $543m appeal for displaced people.
Pakistani troops retook the largest town in the Swat Valley from the Taliban, though they were still meeting pockets of resistance from fighters on the outskirts of the town.

The Taliban have recommenced radio broadcasts and distribute audio and video recordings in Pakistan’s North West Frontier province after a two-month hiatus, while uncertainty remains over whether they were fully pushed out of the Swat Valley.
The US launched its biggest offensive against the Taliban in five years, pouring 4,000 marines into Afghanistan's Helmand province in Operation Khanjar.
A roadside bomb explosion in Afghanistan's southern Helmand province, attributed to Taliban IEDs, killed two US marines and was caught on camera for the first time.

A secret Taliban leadership meeting to choose a successor to Baitullah Mehsud erupted into a gun battle in which at least one commander was killed, according to Pakistani government claims that were denied by the men allegedly involved.
Pakistani Taliban leader Baitullah Mehsud was killed in a CIA missile strike, according to the Pakistani government and a senior Taliban commander.

The Taliban launched a suicide attack on a convoy of foreign soldiers in Kabul, killing one soldier and seven other people and wounding more than 50, less than two days before Afghanistan's presidential election.
Taliban district leader Abdul Rahman is reported to have died in a NATO airstrike in Afghanistan, though the Kunduz Taliban denied the report.

The Pakistan army captured Swat Taliban spokesman Muslim Khan and commander Mahmood Khan, the first arrest of an insurgent leader since the start of a major military offensive in the Swat valley four months earlier.
Pakistani troops captured the key Taliban town of Kotkai, hometown of Pakistani Taliban chief Hakimullah Mehsud, after fierce fighting.
Taliban attacks a UN guesthouse in Kabul, creating a major security problem for the UN.
Taliban commanders held secret exploratory peace talks with a UN special envoy in Dubai.
Taliban militants launch the biggest and most complex assault on Kabul since the fall of the Taliban in 2001, attacking government buildings in a coordinated attack.
British and NATO troops are preparing a major offensive in southern Afghanistan aimed at seizing areas in Helmand province still under Taliban control.
A Taliban spokesman claimed responsibility for a remote-control roadside bomb attack in Lower Dir, Pakistan, that killed three American soldiers and three teenage girls outside a school.

Thousands of British, US and Afghan troops are poised to launch Operation Moshtarak, their biggest joint offensive to push the Taliban out of all major populated areas of Helmand by the end of the year.
Taliban commander in chief Mullah Baradar was arrested in Karachi by the Pakistan army's Inter-Services Intelligence in a joint operation with the CIA.
Nato officials say the focus of international forces will shift from Helmand to Kandahar for a planned summer offensive against the Taliban, with the operation still in the planning stages.
Pakistan refuses to hand over captured Taliban leaders, including deputy leader Abdul Ghani Baradar, to Afghanistan, citing concerns they could be released or transferred to the US.

A senior deputy of the Pakistani Taliban, Qari Hussain Mehsud, claims responsibility for Faisal Shahzad's failed Times Square attack, though army officials and militant experts remain skeptical of the link.
A Taliban suicide car bomber attacked a Nato convoy during rush hour in Kabul, killing 12 Afghan civilians and six foreign troops and injuring dozens.
The commander of US and Nato forces warns that military operations to secure control of Kandahar, the Taliban heartland in southern Afghanistan, will be slower and take longer than first planned.
Amnesty International reports that nearly 4 million Pakistanis live under Taliban rule in the north-western tribal belt, suffering human rights abuses from both militants and the army.
The Taliban leadership publicly announces it will not enter talks with Hamid Karzai or foreign powers until coalition troops withdraw.

A security monitor warns that the US military build-up in Kandahar is likely to strengthen the Taliban's hold and cause a significant rise in support for the armed opposition, as June marked a record for Taliban attacks.
The Afghan Taliban issued a statement rejecting recent claims of US progress in the war, saying attacks were increasing around the capital and in their southern heartland.

On the ninth anniversary of the US-UK invasion of Afghanistan, a remembrance ceremony was held opposite Downing Street, where names of Afghan civilians and British soldiers killed in the war were read, amid opinion polls showing majorities in Britain and Afghanistan support peace negotiations with the Taliban.
The US escalates its assault on the Taliban with increased bombing and missile raids, relaxed rules on destroying civilian property, and the first deployment of M1 Abrams tanks to Afghanistan.
Afghan government and Nato allies were revealed to have been duped into holding peace talks with a man posing as senior Taliban leader Mullah Akhtar Muhammad Mansour.
The Obama administration review said the US had stopped the Taliban's momentum in Afghanistan and would begin withdrawing troops next summer, though it warned gains remained fragile and reversible.
US military campaign in Kandahar has splintered Taliban leadership, forcing senior commanders to flee and reducing two top field commanders to squabbling over footsoldiers, according to residents.

Afghanistan's education minister claims the Taliban leadership is prepared to drop its ban on girls' schools, though the Taliban has not publicly confirmed this and analysts consider an announcement unlikely.
At least 480 Taliban prisoners escaped from Sarpoza prison in Kandahar through a tunnel dug by insurgents over five months.
The Taliban launched a multi-pronged attack on Kandahar involving gunmen and suicide bombers targeting at least five locations, which wounded at least 24 people.
US Defence Secretary Robert Gates confirms preliminary contacts are under way between the US and the Taliban, while stating the Taliban are not yet ready to talk seriously.

Ahmed Wali Karzai, half-brother of Afghan President Hamid Karzai and a key power broker in Kandahar, was killed by a trusted bodyguard; his life had been shaped by the Soviet invasion and the fall of the Taliban regime.
Taliban suicide bombers attacked a government compound in Charikar, Afghanistan, killing 18 people, with a Taliban spokesman claiming credit for the violence.
The Taliban attacked the British Council office in Kabul on Afghanistan's independence day, killing nine people.
An anti-war assembly is planned in Trafalgar Square, with the author arguing that a premature NATO withdrawal could result in a Taliban victory and a bloodbath.
The Taliban claimed responsibility for a car bomb attack in Kabul that killed 13 Americans and four Afghan civilians.
A sectarian suicide bombing in Kabul, the first of its kind in Afghanistan, is disowned by the Taliban, though involvement by elements from different Taliban groups cannot be ruled out.
The Taliban stated they are prepared to open a political office in Qatar.
The Taliban announced they are prepared to open a political office in Qatar for negotiations with the international community, though they did not say when it would happen.

The Obama administration denies a report that it has decided to release high-ranking Taliban officials from Guantanamo Bay in return for the Taliban's agreement to open a political office in Qatar for peace negotiations.

A leaked US military report says the Taliban, backed by Pakistan, are confident they can win the Afghanistan conflict and are gaining popular support, while the Taliban say they have no plans to hold peace talks with the Afghan government in Saudi Arabia.
Afghan President Hamid Karzai confronted Pakistani leadership in Islamabad, demanding that Pakistan bring the Taliban leadership, including Mullah Mohammad Omar, to the negotiating table.
Afghan clerics issue guidelines critics say are reminiscent of the Taliban era and a "green light for Talibanisation," including restrictions on women.
Taliban announced they were suspending peace talks with the US, accusing American negotiators of being "shaky, erratic and vague."
The Taliban launched its largest coordinated attack in Kabul in 11 years, targeting embassies, NATO bases, parliament, and government buildings, with gun battles continuing for hours.
Afghan women are leaving the country and withdrawing from education and work amid fears of a Taliban return and eroding women's rights ahead of the 2014 NATO handover.
A senior Taliban commander, in an interview published in the New Statesman, admits the Taliban cannot win the war in Afghanistan and distances the movement from al-Qaida, calling it a "plague."

A NATO air strike in Afghanistan killed key Pakistani Taliban leader Mullah Dadullah and his deputy Shakir, while a CIA drone strike was reported to have killed Haqqani network operational commander Badruddin Haqqani, though Pakistani officials said they could not confirm his death.
The Taliban shot a 15-year-old girl, Malala Yousafzai, in the head for publicly opposing its ban on girls' schooling.
A Taliban gunman shot 14-year-old Pakistani schoolgirl and peace activist Malala Yousafzai, and the Taliban claimed responsibility for the attack.
The Pakistani Taliban threatened journalists over coverage of their assassination attempt on Malala Yousafzai, prompting several news organizations to take extra security precautions.
A Pakistani schoolgirl shot by the Taliban, Malala Yousafzai, is sent to the UK for specialist treatment.
A Taliban spokesman claimed responsibility for a suicide bomb attack in Buner, Pakistan, that killed anti-Taliban politician Fateh Khan and five other people.
Mullah Mohammed Omar, the Taliban’s undisputed head, died.

Malala Yousafzai, the 15-year-old Pakistani girl shot in the head by the Taliban, was discharged from the Birmingham hospital where she was being treated to continue her rehabilitation as an outpatient.
A US drone strike reportedly killed top Pakistani Taliban commander Mullah Nazir in South Waziristan.

Planned Taliban peace talks in Qatar remain at a stalemate, with no Taliban representatives meeting Afghan President Hamid Karzai during his visit to Doha and Pakistan reportedly backing away from support for the process.

The Taliban announced its annual spring offensive, dubbed Khalid bin Waleed, which will consist of "special military tactics" and "insider attacks" carried out "in a systematic and coordinated manner."
A Taliban-linked group claimed responsibility for a suicide car bombing in Kabul that killed six US troops and civilians and nine Afghan civilians, including two schoolchildren.
A US drone strike reportedly killed Wali ur-Rehman, the deputy leader of the Pakistani Taliban, though the Taliban refused to confirm his death.
A delegation of senior Afghan Taliban members made a historic trip to Iran to meet with officials, a visit likely to worry both Washington and Kabul.

Taliban fighters launched rockets at Kabul's military airport, with seven suicide bombers taking over buildings near the airport before being killed by police, causing no casualties but closing the airport.

The Taliban opened an office in Doha, Qatar, intended as a venue for peace talks, but the display of its flag and plaque as the "Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan" prompted Afghan President Hamid Karzai to pull out of planned negotiations.
The US agrees to open direct talks with Taliban leaders in Doha, Qatar, dropping preconditions for negotiations over Afghanistan's future.
The Taliban announced they are going ahead with opening a political office in Qatar as a base for dialogue, though it remains uncertain whether this leads to peace talks.
The Taliban planned to sit down for peace talks with the US, prompting fear among Afghan women about losing rights.
The US suspended plans to attend peace talks with the Taliban in Doha after Afghan President Hamid Karzai objected to the Taliban portraying itself as a government in exile.

The Taliban's Doha political office, which had been waiting over a year to formally open, sparked a crisis by declaring itself the office of the "Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan," raising its old flag and refusing to say it would talk to the Karzai government.
Taliban attack Kabul's presidential palace.
Taliban insurgents attack a foreign supply compound in Kabul.
Malala Yousafzai delivers a defiant speech at the United Nations on her 16th birthday, responding to the Taliban's attempt to assassinate her in October 2012.

A senior member of the Pakistani Taliban writes an open letter to Malala Yousafzai expressing regret that he did not warn her before the attack but not apologizing, claiming she was targeted for maligning the insurgents.

The Taliban leader Mullah Mohammad Omar issued a five-page message ahead of Eid al-Fitr, accepting a key US demand not to use Afghanistan as a base to threaten other countries, denying the Taliban would seek to monopolise power, favouring an "inclusive government run on Islamic principles," and calling on Afghans to boycott next year's presidential elections.

Former Taliban finance minister Agha Jan Motasim claims in an interview that a majority of Afghan insurgents want to negotiate a peace deal but their views have been suppressed by hardliners controlling the movement's propaganda machine.
Malala Yousafzai, who was shot by the Taliban for promoting female education, urges British girls not to take their schooling for granted in a BBC Panorama programme.
Malala Yousafzai, who survived an assassination attempt by the Taliban, wins the European parliament's Sakharov human rights prize.
A CIA drone strike killed Pakistani Taliban leader Hakimullah Mehsud in North Waziristan, which a Pakistani government minister said destroyed attempts to hold peace talks with the militants.
The Pakistani Taliban selects hardliner Mullah Fazlullah as its new leader following the death of previous leader Hakimullah Mehsud in a drone strike.
Two senior members of the Haqqani network, a Taliban faction, were killed in a US drone strike on a religious seminary in Hangu, Pakistan.

The Taliban claimed responsibility for shooting down a helicopter in Zabul province, Afghanistan, though Nato and Afghan officials said the crash, which killed six US soldiers, appeared to be caused by a mechanical fault.

A Taliban splinter group, Fidai Mahaz, claimed responsibility for killing British-Swedish journalist Nils Horner in Kabul, accusing him of being an MI6 spy, though it offered no proof and other insurgent groups denied involvement.
Taliban militants attacked a luxury hotel in Kabul, killing nine people including four foreigners, and also assaulted a police station in Jalalabad, killing 11 people.
The Taliban claimed responsibility for a suicide attack on an aid agency in Kabul that killed one child and a driver and injured five people.
The Taliban began its annual spring offensive with a series of attacks across Afghanistan that killed at least a dozen people.

The US warned that Afghanistan would lose American financial and security support if a candidate illegally took power amid an election dispute, while noting the Taliban continues to hold territory in the south and east.
The Australian government said it would investigate the reported kidnapping and torture by the Taliban of an Afghan Hazara asylum seeker, Zainullah Naseri, who was deported from Australia in August.
Malala Yousafzai, who was shot by Taliban gunmen in 2012, is announced as a co-recipient of the Nobel peace prize.
A second Afghan Hazara was deported from Australia weeks after the first deported Hazara man, Zainullah Naseri, was kidnapped and tortured by the Taliban.
US forces in Afghanistan will receive expanded powers to target Taliban fighters threatening their safety or that of Afghan officials, under an order from Barack Obama.
Oxfam warns that Afghan women risk being excluded from peace talks with the Taliban, threatening hard-won rights gains.
Taliban militants launched a spate of attacks across Afghanistan, killing 19 Afghans and two foreign soldiers since Friday evening.
Five Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan fighters, some believed involved in the December 2014 Peshawar school massacre, were arrested inside Afghanistan.

Afghanistan's main spy agency announced it has detained the commander of the Taliban splinter group Mahaz-e-Fedaiyan for the murder of journalist Nils Horner, though the Swedish embassy said the arrest took it by surprise and Swedish Radio said the information remains uncertain.
Afghan President Ashraf Ghani told key aides that formal talks between the Afghan government and the Taliban will begin in the coming weeks, though the Taliban spokesman denied any plans for talks.
Taliban gunmen attacked a Kabul guesthouse, killing at least 14 people, in the most audacious assault by the insurgents in the Afghan capital since the start of their spring offensive.
A message claimed to be from Taliban leader Mullah Omar endorsed recent peace talks between the Taliban and Afghan government officials, though its veracity was not confirmed.

News reports raise the possibility that Taliban leader Mullah Omar died years earlier, though it remains unconfirmed and some suggest he could still be alive, with potential implications for Taliban unity and peace talks.
Mullah Akhtar Mansoor is believed to be the Taliban's new leader, succeeding Mullah Omar, though his grip on power remains uncertain amid rival claims.
The Taliban confirmed the death of Mullah Mohammad Omar and announced Mullah Akhtar Mansoor as its new leader, amid internal dispute over the coverup and succession.

A Taliban suicide bomber dressed in police uniform detonated an explosives vest outside a police academy in Kabul, one of a wave of attacks that killed more than 40 people in the deadliest 24 hours in the Afghan capital in years.
Taliban forces overran the Musa Qala district centre in northern Helmand, Afghanistan, a victory celebrated by the group as a propaganda boost.
The Taliban claim to have resolved a leadership rift as key figures from Mullah Omar's family swore allegiance to new leader Mullah Akhtar Mansoor.
The Taliban captured the northern Afghan city of Kunduz, the first major city to come under Taliban control since 2001.
The Taliban captured the Afghan city of Kunduz, marking their first seizure of a major urban center since 2001 and dealing a significant military and political blow to the Afghan government.
A US airstrike hit a Médecins Sans Frontières trauma centre in Kunduz, Afghanistan, amid fighting after the Taliban swept through the city, killing at least 30 people.
The Taliban withdrew from the northern Afghan city of Kunduz two weeks after seizing it, describing the retreat as a tactical withdrawal.

Aware Girls, a women-led organization in Peshawar, continues its work opposing the Taliban through education and a peace network, despite ongoing violence including the Taliban's December 2014 school attack that killed 132 children and 18 adults.
Taliban gains ground in Afghanistan, prompting an exodus of Afghans leaving the country, with the capture of Kunduz cited as a trigger for departures.
Afghan Taliban leader Mullah Akhtar Mansoor was seriously wounded in a gunfight during a meeting outside Quetta, Pakistan, according to the Afghan government.
Taliban fighters attacked Kandahar airport, killing dozens of civilians and one soldier in the deadliest ever attack on the largest military facility in southern Afghanistan.
The Taliban launched a major assault on the Helmand town of Sangin after months of steady military advance that put more than half of the province under their control.
The Taliban launched a fierce attack on government buildings in Sangin district, Helmand province, killing nine soldiers, wounding seven, and capturing three, as part of an intensified assault.
A US drone strike killed Taliban leader Mullah Akhtar Mansoor while he was travelling in Pakistan’s Balochistan province, an attack the Taliban confirmed.
The Taliban proclaimed Mullah Haibatullah Akhundzadah as their new emir, days after a US drone killed former chief Mullah Akhtar Mansoor.

Former Afghan President Hamid Karzai warns that US airstrikes against the Taliban are undermining Afghan security and fueling conflict, after the Taliban captured large swaths of territory in Helmand.
The Afghan army rushed reinforcements to Helmand province as Taliban militants closed in on Lashkar Gah after capturing most of Nad Ali and Nawa districts.
More than a hundred US troops have been sent to Lashkar Gah to help prevent the Taliban from overrunning the capital of Afghanistan's Helmand province.

Taliban double bombing near Afghanistan's defence ministry in Kabul killed at least 24 people and wounded scores more, with Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid claiming the defence ministry was the target of the first attack and police the second.
A US airstrike accidentally killed at least seven Afghan police officers in Uruzgan during operations to help Afghan forces repel a Taliban offensive near Tarin Kot.

The Taliban and Afghan government representatives restarted secret talks in Qatar in September and October, the first known negotiations since a Pakistan-brokered process broke down after Mullah Akhtar Mansoor’s death.
Senior members of the Taliban's political commission based in Qatar travelled to Pakistan for discussions with security officials there about possible peace talks with the Afghan government.
The Taliban claimed responsibility for an explosion at Bagram Airfield in Afghanistan that caused multiple casualties.

The Afghan Taliban are facing a cash crisis as donors are unwilling to fund an insurgency whose victims are increasingly civilians rather than foreign troops, according to several members of the movement.

The US military confirmed that 33 civilians were killed during a special forces raid targeting two senior Taliban commanders in Kunduz, Afghanistan, in November 2016, but ruled that US troops acted in self-defense.
The Taliban killed at least 38 people and wounded dozens more in a suicide bomb attack on a bus carrying government employees in Kabul.
Malala Yousafzai, who was shot by the Taliban in 2012 for advocating girls' education, wins a place at the University of Oxford to study philosophy, politics and economics.
Between 2001 and 2009, the Taliban destroyed or damaged 401 schools in Pakistan's Swat valley, about 70 percent of them girls' schools.
Malala Yousafzai, a 14-year-old girl shot by the Taliban, arrives at a hospital.
Malala Yousafzai gives her first interview since being shot by the Taliban.

facts.text: In 2001, the Taliban government in Afghanistan crumbled as Northern Alliance forces entered Kabul, and Mullah Omar vanished from view as US and Afghan forces toppled his government.
On 2007-02-15, George Bush ordered 3,200 extra US troops to Afghanistan in expectation of a spring offensive against a resurgent Taliban.
On 2007-08-24, the UK Ministry of Defence confirmed three British soldiers died from friendly fire when American F15 warplanes bombed them during a clash with Taliban fighters in Helmand.
On 2009-03-30, heavily armed men in police uniforms stormed a police academy in Pakistan, killing 11 and injuring nearly 100, an attack claimed by Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan leader Baitullah Masud.
On 2009-04-23, Taliban fighters swept across Buner district, occupying government buildings and forcing local police to retreat, as Hillary Clinton warned of a "mortal threat" to world security.

On 2012-07-05, a senior Taliban commander, in an interview published in the New Statesman, admitted the Taliban cannot win the war in Afghanistan and distanced the movement from al-Qaida, calling it a "plague."

On 2014-03-11, Taliban splinter group Fidai Mahaz claimed responsibility for killing British-Swedish journalist Nils Horner in Kabul, accusing him of being an MI6 spy, though it offered no proof and other insurgent groups denied involvement.

On 2015-01-30, Afghanistan's main spy agency announced it detained the commander of Taliban splinter group Mahaz-e-Fedaiyan for the murder of journalist Nils Horner, though the Swedish embassy was surprised and Swedish Radio said the information remains uncertain.

event-551ad409a1a078fa.summary: Taliban fighters attacked Kandahar airport, killing dozens of civilians and one soldier in the deadliest ever attack on the largest military facility in southern Afghanistan.

event-f461594975367589.summary: The Taliban launched a major assault on the Helmand town of Sangin after months of steady military advance that put more than half of the province under their control.

event-3e88caf05afc48d7.summary: The Taliban launched a fierce attack on government buildings in Sangin district, Helmand province, killing nine soldiers, wounding seven, and capturing three, as part of an intensified assault.

event-76e35de4066bd8db.summary: A US drone strike killed Taliban leader Mullah Akhtar Mansoor while he was travelling in Pakistan’s Balochistan province, an attack the Taliban confirmed.

event-2e76bc18cc50b5e7.summary: The Taliban proclaimed Mullah Haibatullah Akhundzadah as their new emir, days after a US drone killed former chief Mullah Akhtar Mansoor.

event-b4ad5b0c09708020.summary: Former Afghan President Hamid Karzai warns that US airstrikes against the Taliban are undermining Afghan security and fueling conflict, after the Taliban captured large swaths of territory in Helmand.

event-60abefcf0ff0abf0.summary: The Afghan army rushed reinforcements to Helmand province as Taliban militants closed in on Lashkar Gah after capturing most of Nad Ali and Nawa districts.

event-b8ab6f7d6720a298.summary: More than a hundred US troops have been sent to Lashkar Gah to help prevent the Taliban from overrunning the capital of Afghanistan's Helmand province.

event-0b18f8eb322ac14b.summary: Taliban double bombing near Afghanistan's defence ministry in Kabul killed at least 24 people and wounded scores more, with Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid claiming the defence ministry was the target of the first attack and police the second.

event-05aa234ec7b7da3c.summary: A US airstrike accidentally killed at least seven Afghan police officers in Uruzgan during operations to help Afghan forces repel a Taliban offensive near Tarin Kot.

event-dea97de1021c36d8.summary: The Taliban and Afghan government representatives restarted secret talks in Qatar in September and October, the first known negotiations since a Pakistan-brokered process broke down after Mullah Akhtar Mansoor’s death.

event-173466a17f85eca5.summary: Senior members of the Taliban's political commission based in Qatar travelled to Pakistan for discussions with security officials there about possible peace talks with the Afghan government.

event-9eddffa986ade888.summary: The Taliban claimed responsibility for an explosion at Bagram Airfield in Afghanistan that caused multiple casualties.

event-57f3655f45dad811.summary: The Afghan Taliban are facing a cash crisis as donors are unwilling to fund an insurgency whose victims are increasingly civilians rather than foreign troops, according to several members of the movement.

event-9407d0f464a85a9c.summary: The US military confirmed that 33 civilians were killed during a special forces raid targeting two senior Taliban commanders in Kunduz, Afghanistan, in November 2016, but ruled that US troops acted in self-defense.

event-0e1578cf7deff4f8.summary: The Taliban killed at least 38 people and wounded dozens more in a suicide bomb attack on a bus carrying government employees in Kabul.

event-722a4975deb6305e.summary: Malala Yousafzai, who was shot by the Taliban in 2012 for advocating girls' education, wins a place at the University of Oxford to study philosophy, politics and economics.

event-01e89b6b0ef82cd4.summary: Between 2001 and 2009, the Taliban destroyed or damaged 401 schools in Pakistan's Swat valley, about 70 percent of them girls' schools.

event-640bee03aa1a0984.summary: Malala Yousafzai, a 14-year-old girl shot by the Taliban, arrives at a hospital.

event-fa892cac28d2d8fb.summary: Malala Yousafzai gives her first interview since being shot by the Taliban.

Afghan defence officials claimed Taliban fighters occupying villages near Kandahar were forced to retreat by a major Afghan and Canadian Nato offensive, though Nato gave a more cautious assessment and did not confirm the death toll.
Nato and Afghan forces killed 20 Taliban fighters in a major offensive on the outskirts of Kandahar, as British paratroopers deployed to the city to deter a potential Taliban threat.

Taliban forces destroyed bridges and laid mines near Kandahar, prompting more than 4,000 people to flee villages and leading Afghan and Canadian forces to move into the region in anticipation of an attack.
The Taliban launched a multi-pronged attack on Kandahar involving gunmen and suicide bombers targeting at least five locations, which wounded at least 24 people.

A senior deputy of the Pakistani Taliban, Qari Hussain Mehsud, claims responsibility for Faisal Shahzad's failed Times Square attack, though army officials and militant experts remain skeptical of the link.
Taliban militants attacked Kandahar's main prison with a truck bomb and freed up to 1,000 prisoners, including 400 Taliban fighters.
